about: Shape recognition for draw-and-hold (docs/dev/handwriting.md 'What the user sees' and 'Client': frontend/src/ink/shapes.js recognise). Each case is one stroke as the layer holds it when the hold timer fires: `samples` are page points at scale 1 (pdf.js viewport, y down), each [x, y, p, t] with x, y in pt to 0.01, p the decoded pressure 0..1 and t integer ms since the first sample; the positive cases end with the pen held still (a 350 ms tail of sub-pixel wobble), as a real hold does. `k` is the layer's scale, css px per pt, for the thresholds given in screen pixels. `expect` is null when recognise must return null, else {kind, params, tol?}: `kind` must match exactly; every numeric key of `params` must match within `tol` points (default 2), except `n` (exact) and `angle` (degrees, within 5°, compared modulo the shape's symmetry: 90 for a rect, 360/n for a polygon, 180 for an ellipse). Params per kind: line and arrow {x1, y1, x2, y2} from the first endpoint to the last (an arrow's x2, y2 is its tip, `head` the mean barb length), rect {cx, cy, w, h, angle} with w along the angle direction and angle in [-45, 45) (0 after an axis snap), triangle {x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3} in the order drawn starting with the corner nearest the first sample, polygon {cx, cy, r, n, angle} with r the circumradius and angle the direction of the first corner in [0, 360/n), circle {cx, cy, r}, ellipse {cx, cy, rx, ry, angle} with rx >= ry and angle in [0, 180). frontend/tests/shapes.test.mjs runs recognise(samples as {x, y, p, t}, {k}) on each case; backend/tests/test_shared_fixtures.py only checks each case's shape and that the stroke a recognised shape is stored as parses on the server (the server never recognises). `tool` lists drags of the Shapes tool (frontend/src/ink/shapeTool.js toolShape(kind, from, to, {shift, k})): `from` is the down point and `to` the pointer at the lift, [x, y] in page points, `k` the layer's css px per pt and `shift` whether Shift is held. `expect` is null when the drag is under 4 css px (hypot(dx, dy) * k < 4: nothing is drawn), else `params`, the shape record's params exactly (each number on the 1/100 pt grid, rounded as Math.round(v * 100) / 100), `count`, how many samples shapes.js shapeSamples gives those params (the dense polyline the stroke commits as: two for a line; tail, tip and both barbs for an arrow; the corners with a sample every 2 pt, closed, for a rectangle; one every 2 pt of perimeter and at least 48, closed, for an ellipse), and `closed`, whether its last sample is its first. The rules: a line or an arrow runs from `from` to `to` (an arrow's tip at `to`, written without `head`, which shapes.js then draws as min(length / 4, 24)), Shift turning its direction about `from` to the nearest 15° with its length kept; a rectangle is {cx, cy, w, h, angle: 0}, the box `from` and `to` span; an ellipse is the one inscribed in that box, {cx, cy, rx, ry, angle} with rx >= ry (angle 0 when the box is at least as wide as it is tall, else 90 with rx half its height); with Shift both take the square box whose side is the larger of |dx| and |dy|, laid from `from` toward `to` (a square, and a circle with rx = ry and angle 0). frontend/tests/shapeTool.test.mjs runs toolShape and shapeSamples on every drag; backend/tests/test_shared_fixtures.py checks each drag's shape and that the stroke it commits (pen false, brush monoline, written xyt, its shape record) parses on the server.

cases.note: a line drawn 1° off horizontal snaps to 0°, about its midpoint
a line drawn 43.6° snaps to 45°
a line drawn 89° snaps vertical
a line at 30° keeps its angle: no axis within 5°
a line at 50° keeps its angle (5° past 45)
zoomed in (k = 2.5) a line is still a line; thresholds are in points
a rectangle drawn 1.5° askew, closed 3 pt short, snaps to the axes
sides 156 and 150 (within 10 %) make a square of their mean
a triangle: three corners in the order drawn, the first nearest the first sample
a regular hexagon, first corner due east
a regular pentagon started at its top: angle -90 normalises to 54 (mod 72)
a circle with 1.5 % radial wobble, closed 8° short
an axis-aligned ellipse 2:1
an ellipse tilted 30°
an arrow: shaft tail to tip, then tip to one barb, back to the tip, and to the other barb
the letter l: a narrow open loop with tails is nothing
a zigzag is open and alternates its turns: never a polygon
an open 120° arc is neither a line nor an ellipse
a tick under 18 pt is too short to be anything, hold or not
the letter S: smooth, open, no corners

tool.note: a line from the down point to the lift: two samples
Shift turns a line in 15° steps about its start, its length kept: 14° becomes 15°
an arrow points from the down point to the lift, its head left to shapes.js (min(length / 4, 24), here 17.75): tail to tip, then the barbs in the same polyline
Shift turns an arrow in 15° steps too: 26.6° becomes 30°
a rectangle spans the down point and the lift, axis-aligned (angle 0): its corners with a sample every 2 pt, closed
a rectangle dragged up and to the left is the same rectangle
Shift makes a square of the longer side, from the down point toward the pointer
Shift's square follows the drag's direction: up and to the left
an ellipse fills the dragged box, rx along its longer side: at least 48 samples, one every 2 pt, closed
a box taller than wide gives an ellipse at 90° (rx >= ry, as recognise returns them)
Shift makes a circle (rx = ry, angle 0) of the longer side, from the down point toward the pointer
Shift's circle follows the drag's direction: up and to the left
a small ellipse still has its 48 samples
every number on the 1/100 pt grid
a drag under 4 css px draws nothing: 2.24 pt at 4/3 css px per pt is 2.98 px
the 4 px floor is measured on screen: the same 2.24 pt at 2 css px per pt is 4.47 px, a line
